## The question

[Quadratic Equations Vertex/Standard Form](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/2479220/quadratic-equations-vertex-standard-form), asked by [Vincent Nguyen](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/493118/vincent-nguyen) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2017-10-18; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> At the moment I'm being taught how to convert Vertex Form into Standard form and Standard Form to Vertex. Now my last assigned problem has been a problem for me, we never went over this in class(Algebra), so I'd love for you to teach me.
>
> >To line an irrigation ditch, a farmer will use rectangular metal
> sheets. Each side will be bent x feet from the edge at an angle
> of 90° to form the trough. If the sheets are 20 ft wide, how far
> from the edge (x) should the farmer bend them to maximize
> the area of a cross-section of the trough.
>
> The formulas I've learnt now are: 
> $$y=f(x)=ax^2+bx+c$$
> $$y=f(h)=a(b(x-h))^2+k$$
> $$h=\frac{-b}{2a}$$
>
> I think I need to find x, but I don't know how to get there using everything I've learned so far, so please help me with this one.
:::

The cross section of the ditch will be a rectangle, lined on the vertical sides and bottom by the metal but open at the top.  If the bend is made $x$ feet from the edge, the two sides will have length $x$ while the bottom will have length $20-2x$.  So the area of the cross section is
$$f(x) = x(20-2x) = 20x-2x^2$$
The graph of $f$ is a parabola.  According to your formula, the vertex of that parabola is at $(5,50)$.
